thread:
Maya Chen: quick PSA — the recurring eng sync invite is showing the organizer's PST timezone for everyone. EU folks see it as 19:00 and APAC as 03:00, which is... unpleasant. Zoom link also seems to have come from last week's duplicate and failed for Maria. Can we fix the recurring invite and make sure the Zoom link is stable?

Alex Rivera: ugh, saw that too. I joined the wrong meeting yesterday because the link was stale.

Li Zhang: is this the case where the event was created with "Use organizer timezone" vs explicit tz on the event? I can take a look.

Maya Chen: thanks Li. I'm guessing the creator created a recurring event in their local tz and didn't set an explicit event timezone. Could we standardize on creating events with the meeting's primary timezone set and set the Zoom link to the meeting series (not a one-off link)?

Jordan Patel: +1. For multi-region teams I'd rather we either rotate times or have two recurring invites (Americas / EMEA+APAC) than force a weird time on somebody every week.

Samir Khan: short-term fix: organizer can duplicate the recurring event and set the timezone explicitly, then delete the broken series. Steps:
```
1) Open event > Edit
2) More actions > Duplicate
3) In the duplicated event, click the time zone next to the time and set to e.g. "London (GMT+1)" or add a secondary TZ
4) Update conferencing to use the Meeting Series link (persistent room)
5) Save and send updates
```
This keeps a stable Zoom link and fixes how it displays for attendees.

Alex Rivera: is there a way to stop Google from shifting times for recurring events across DST boundaries? That bit confuses people.

Li Zhang: Google will keep the same clock time in the selected timezone, but if attendees' calendars are in a different tz they'll see the converted time. For DST edge cases, the safe route is to pick the timezone that anchors the event and mention local conversions in the event description.

Maya Chen: proposal: for RFC/design review weekly syncs we do either: 1) rotate meeting times monthly (Americas-friendly one month, EMEA-friendly next), OR 2) create 2 mirrored recurring events with the same agenda and separate Zoom rooms. Which do folks prefer?

Jordan Patel: I'd vote for mirrored events for predictable attendance — fewer people miss because of midnight starts.

Samir Khan: mirrored events = more calendar noise tho. Maybe we can do mirrored events but add a single canonical agenda doc and mark one as the primary (agenda & recording).

Alex Rivera: also, can we set the calendar event to disable "guests can modify" so people don't accidentally edit the series? Seen that break a few times.

Maya Chen: good call. We'll disable guest edits for the series and use shareable doc for agenda. I'll:
- create mirrored recurring events for the eng sync (Americas / EMEA+APAC)
- set persistent Zoom meeting IDs for both and pin them in the calendar description
- disable guest edits and include the canonical agenda link
- add a note about rotating times monthly if attendance drops
I'll make the change today and post updates here.

calendar-bot: Reminder: Zoom link for meeting series "Eng Sync (Americas)" expires in 12 days.

Maya Chen: thanks @calendar-bot — I'll renew the meeting series link when I create the new invites.

zoom-bot: New persistent meeting created: Meeting ID 987-654-321. Link added to event description.

Li Zhang: LMK when done and I'll check the EMEA attendees' view, and Samir can verify recording permissions.

Samir Khan: will do. Also can we add a line in the invite: "If this time is impossible for you regularly, ping #eng-platform and we can rotate" — keeps the line of communication open. :thumbsup: 

Maya Chen: done. Created two recurring events and updated descriptions with both meeting IDs + canonical agenda. Sent updates to all attendees. If anyone still sees the old one, try removing the series from your calendar and re-adding.

Alex Rivera: confirmed — shows correctly for me now (10:00 PT / 18:00 GMT). Thanks! :tada:

Jordan Patel: looks good for EMEA too. Thanks Maya.

Maya Chen: closing the loop here. If we see more noise, we'll trial rotation. Appreciate the quick responses.
